title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

errors: The equivalence 'T ≪ T' (T<T', not abutting) ⟺ ∃x with T⊂L_{<x}, T'⊂L_{>x}' fails when L is not dense. Take a<b consecutive (a jump), a∈T, b∈T'. They do not abut in the stated sense (a≠b), yet no separating x exists. Either 'raccordement' must also cover jumps, or L must be assumed dense or completed (e.g. boundary points taken in a completion). The next page restates the conditions somewhat differently, apparently sensing this.
The last line as written reads 'T⊂L_{≤a}', mixing a fixed endpoint a with the quantified x. It is clearly meant to be T⊂L_{<x} (the next page writes it this way).

Minor gap: the existence of a greatest element of ∂T is asserted from 'T is a ps. tr.' without justification. It depends on how ∂ is defined for unbounded intervals, e.g. whether endpoints in a completion such as ±∞ or ∂L are counted.

ideas.what: Intersection of pseudo-intervals in moderate position is a pseudo-interval, with boundary contained in the union of the boundaries
ideas.modern_name: convex subsets of a linear order are closed under intersection; endpoints of an intersection

ideas.what: Strict 'entirely to the left' order on disjoint pseudo-intervals, distinct from inclusion
ideas.modern_name: interval order / precedence order on disjoint convex sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; interval orders studied by Wiener (1914) and Fishburn (1970)

ideas.what: Distinguishing abutting ('raccordement') from separated pairs of intervals; strengthened relation ≪ via a separating point
ideas.modern_name: adjacency vs separation of intervals; gaps and jumps in linear orders

missed.claim: This page is part of an elementary, order-theoretic foundation for 'networks via cuttings' (réseaux via découpages) built on a one-dimensional base. It is loosely related to Grothendieck's tame-topology ('topologie modérée') program in the Esquisse. The page itself contains only routine order theory; the possible interest lies in the overall program, not in this page.
missed.quote: On va introduire une relation (pas l'inclusion !) d'ordre entre ps-tronçons
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck set up combinatorial foundations for cut-up spaces in 1986. This may interest historians of the tame-topology and dessins/réseaux circle of ideas, but it carries no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary order theory of intervals in a totally ordered set (convexity, precedence order, abutting vs separated). It is correct up to a small density gap, and is preparatory to defining interstitial intervals. Nothing here is unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'Position relation' should read 'Position relative de raccordement' (the struck word is 'impropre').
The margin note reads roughly: 'Cela veut dire que T, T' en pos. rel. mod. et T∩T'=∅'.
In the line 'il s'ensuit que … a un plus grand élément a', the subject is ∂T; the struck fragment is likely '∂T≠∅'.
The final equivalence should read ∃x∈L tel que T⊂L_{<x}, T'⊂L_{>x}, not 'L_{≤a}'.
The relation symbol in the definition is written as ≺ / ≼ (curly) in the display and as < afterwards; it denotes the same strict precedence relation.
